summary: First worldwide conviction for Syrian state torture. Life sentence for 27 murders, 4,000+ torture victims.

title: Judgment — Eyad Al-Gharib convicted as accomplice
summary: Co-defendant convicted of aiding crimes against humanity (4.5 years). First-ever verdict for Syrian regime crimes worldwide.

title: Judgment — Life imprisonment for complicity in crimes against humanity
summary: First French conviction for Liberian civil war crimes. Life sentence for complicity in CAH including torture and acts of barbarism in Lofa County (1993-1994).

title: Appeal — Life sentence confirmed
summary: Appeal court confirmed the life sentence in full. Civitas Maxima and GJRP evidence upheld.

title: Cour de cassation du Sénégal — Souleymane Guengueng et autres c. Hissène Habré
summary: Senegalese Court of Cassation upheld dismissal of the initial criminal complaint, holding that Senegalese courts lacked jurisdiction over crimes committed abroad — triggering the long international campaign that followed.

title: Guengueng et al. v. Senegal — UN Committee Against Torture (CAT/C/36/D/181/2001)
summary: CAT found Senegal in violation of Articles 5(2) and 7 of the Convention Against Torture for failing to prosecute or extradite Habré. Foundational decision on the aut dedere aut judicare obligation.

title: ECOWAS Court of Justice — Hissein Habré c. République du Sénégal (ECW/CCJ/JUD/06/10)
summary: ECOWAS Court ruled that prosecuting Habré under retroactively amended Senegalese law would violate non-retroactivity (nullum crimen sine lege), and recommended a special ad hoc international tribunal — directly leading to the creation of the Extraordinary African Chambers.

title: ICJ — Questions Relating to the Obligation to Prosecute or Extradite (Belgium v. Senegal)
summary: ICJ held Senegal breached Articles 6(2) and 7(1) of the Convention Against Torture by failing to submit the Habré case to its competent authorities for prosecution. Landmark ICJ ruling on the erga omnes partes obligation to prosecute torture.

title: EAC — Statute of the Extraordinary African Chambers (Senegal–AU Agreement)
summary: Constitutive statute creating the Extraordinary African Chambers within Senegalese courts to try international crimes committed in Chad between 1982 and 1990 — implementation of the ICJ ruling.

title: EAC — Indictment / Ordonnance de renvoi (Chambre d'instruction)
summary: Order committing Habré for trial on charges of crimes against humanity, war crimes and torture after a 19-month investigation, more than 2,500 witnesses interviewed.

title: EAC Trial Judgment — Life imprisonment for crimes against humanity, war crimes, and torture
summary: First conviction of a former head of state by the courts of another country under universal jurisdiction. Life sentence for CAH, war crimes, torture, and rape as crime against humanity (1982–1990).
english_translation_source: Bilingual FR/EN summaries at chambresafricaines.org and legal-tools.org

title: EAC Trial Chamber — Reparations Judgment
summary: Trial chamber ordered individual reparations to 7,396 named victims (10–20 million CFA francs each) and tasked the AU Trust Fund with collective reparations.

title: EAC Appeals Chamber — Appeal Judgment
summary: Appeals Chamber confirmed conviction and life sentence; partially modified reparations. Definitively closes the criminal phase, 26 years after victims first filed complaints.
